title: Before any statistic: why should Brent and WTI be linked?
rubric: Names the mechanism: both are light sweet crudes; if one gets too cheap relative to the other (net of transport and quality), traders ship / refiners substitute — arbitrage ties the prices.
Says the link is through the spread, bounded by transport and logistics costs — not a fixed price ratio of exactly one.
Predicts the statistical signature: daily returns strongly correlated; levels moving together with a spread that fluctuates but does not drift away for good.
Lists what can weaken or break the link: pipeline / storage bottlenecks at the delivery point, export restrictions, freight shocks, regional supply events (e.g. a hurricane).
Explains why coffee is a useful control: no mechanism links it to crude, so any 'relationship' found in levels would have to be spurious.
States that the mechanism comes first because a statistical link without a mechanism is fragile and probably spurious.
